source_review.notes: Checked all ten final official NASA, DOE, FAA, and Acquisition.gov references on 2026-08-31; every final URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed NASA lifecycle systems engineering, alternative evaluation, cost-effectiveness, and Cost Estimating Handbook material; DOE lifecycle cost and estimate-development guidance; FAA acquisition safety-risk guidance in its stated domain context; and the current FAR lifecycle-cost definition. The chapter does not generalize FAA governance to other domains or claim compliance with any source.

evidence: Reviewed feasible-set definition using mandatory constraint functions g_j(a) <= 0.
Reviewed discounted lifecycle-cost expressions, residual-value sign, valuation horizon, and cost-element indices.
Reviewed real/nominal consistency relation 1+i=(1+r)(1+pi).
Reviewed conditional reliability notation, Pareto dominance, and conditional additive value model.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols are defined before decision use; feasibility, monetary value, reliability, safety risk, and preference are kept as distinct constructs.

evidence: Executed reliability-safety-lifecycle-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-070/report.json.
Recomputed five-year NPVs at 4% as A=234.64, B=205.81, C=202.24, and D=215.94.
Confirmed A is gate-infeasible, B is dominated by C, and the two-attribute frontier is C,D.
Recomputed Example 2 three-year lifecycle costs as X=181.70 and Y=177.23, a 4.47 difference after rounding.
Recomputed the nominal consistency rate from 4% real and 3% inflation as 7.12%.
Recomputed Exercise 2 four-year lifecycle costs as A=207.12 and B=210.19, a 3.07 difference after rounding.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All arithmetic uses synthetic point inputs. Discounted included cost does not establish complete cost, affordability, safety, reliability, preference, or production performance.

evidence: Confirmed that hard-constraint feasibility precedes compensating comparison.
Confirmed the residual value is subtracted only when realizable and consistently bounded.
Confirmed Pareto dominance requires no-worse performance on every included attribute and strict improvement on at least one.
Confirmed expected scenario cost requires coherent probabilities and does not imply a safety criterion.
Confirmed additive utility is explicitly conditional on cardinal value functions, weights, independence, and external constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulas are decision models under declared assumptions, not proofs of correctness, compliance, risk tolerability, or optimality in an unmodeled system.

evidence: Challenged failed and inconclusive safety gates, all-options-infeasible cases, affordability peaks, and mandatory versus enhancing criteria.
Reviewed incomplete boundaries, inconsistent horizons, acquisition-price anchoring, real/nominal mixing, double counting, transfers, externalities, and residual value.
Reviewed sparse failure data, repair tails, downtime thresholds, correlated drivers, catastrophic scenarios, and invalid ordinal arithmetic.
Reviewed redundancy common cause, coverage, dormant failure, proof tests, post-failure load, maintenance-induced error, and false trips.
Reviewed supplier exit, obsolescence, data/IP rights, staffing, facilities, verification/certification, incident response, and disposal.
Reviewed all ten worked examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production use requires domain safety/regulatory, mission/business, operator/maintainer, reliability/statistical, cost/finance, human-factors, supplier/logistics, security, legal, independent verification, technical-authority, and acceptance review.

evidence: Confirmed noncompensable safety, compliance, prohibited-outcome, and minimum mission gates remain outside scalar scores.
Confirmed alternatives share cost boundary, configuration maturity, horizon, price basis, rate convention, and outcome definitions.
Confirmed lifecycle scope includes development through disposal or records exclusions explicitly.
Confirmed reliability and safety inputs retain mission, environment, demand, maintenance, coverage, dependency, common-cause, and uncertainty conditions.
Confirmed expected values do not replace tails, constraints, distributional effects, or acceptance authority.
Confirmed estimates preserve baseline variance and update with actual/configuration evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: No purchase price, NPV, weighted score, point availability, expected downtime, vendor statement, or sunk expenditure is presented as sufficient decision evidence.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents constrained decision models and recomputable arithmetic but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: The executable result is labeled synthetic_costs_constraints_and_point_availability_only.
The fixture explicitly disclaims investment, safety, reliability, and production-estimate conclusions.
Source-backed guidance is attributed without claiming local compliance, approval, or universal governance.
Field, supplier, quote, failure, repair, and workload evidence is treated as conditional on configuration and context.
No external review, certification, achieved safety, risk acceptance, or production cost validation is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic arithmetic, current-source review, internal engineering review, and real-system assurance remain explicitly separated.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked lifecycle cost, affordability, reliability, availability, safety risk, alternatives, NPV, Pareto dominance, sensitivity, uncertainty, residual risk, value of information, sunk cost, and noncompensation.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked decision framing, technical baselines, cost boundaries and time profiles, reliability and safety-control causality, common cause, supportability, uncertainty/correlation, affordability, supplier exit, option value, VoI, actual-cost updates, authority, dissent, and re-open triggers.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from gate-first framing through whole-life estimation, reliability/safety mechanisms, dominance and preference, uncertainty, evidence, and governance. Ten distinct examples and five complete answers include arithmetic, counterexamples, failure cases, design comparisons, field updates, and unfamiliar transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/DOE/FAA/GSA expert, regulator, domain safety engineer, mission or business owner, operator or maintainer, reliability statistician, cost estimator or financial authority, human-factors specialist, supplier or logistics owner, cybersecurity specialist, legal counsel, independent verification reviewer, technical authority, or residual-risk acceptance authority review is claimed.
